recipes.name: Homemade Nut and Seed Granola
recipes.summary: Crunchy oven granola with almonds, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, flax and dried cranberries.
steps: Heat the oven to 325°F and line the baking sheet with parchment.
Mix the oats, almonds, pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds, flaxseed, cinnamon and salt in a large bowl.
Warm the maple syrup and oil together for 20 seconds, stir in the vanilla, and pour over the oats. Stir until everything is coated.
Spread on the sheet and press down lightly. Bake 25 to 30 minutes, stirring once halfway, until golden.
Cool completely on the pan without stirring, about 30 minutes, so it forms clusters. Break up and stir in the cranberries.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 2 weeks in an airtight jar at room temperature.
recipes.kids: Kids can stir the oats and break up the clusters. Whole nuts and seeds are a choking risk for children under 4; chop them fine or leave them out.

swaps.nut_free: Use more pumpkin and sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a batch for the week.

recipes.name: Homemade Trail Mix
recipes.summary: Peanuts, cashews, almonds, seeds and raisins, mixed your way. A sturdy snack for hikes and car trips.
steps: Stir everything together in a bowl.
Portion into snack bags or keep in a jar.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 1 month in an airtight jar.

freezer.text: Freeze up to 3 months to keep the nuts fresh.

recipes.kids: Whole nuts and seeds are a choking risk for children under 4; chop them fine or leave them out. Check that school snacks follow any nut-free rules.

swaps.nut_free: Use only sunflower and pumpkin seeds, plus pretzels and dried fruit.

recipes.name: Oatmeal Raisin Walnut Cookies
recipes.summary: Chewy, cinnamon-spiced oatmeal cookies loaded with raisins and walnuts.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line the baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the butter and both sugars until creamy. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, baking soda, cinnamon and salt, then the oats, raisins and walnuts.
Scoop rounded tablespoons 2 inches apart on the sheets. Bake one sheet at a time, 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are golden and the centers look a little soft.
Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then move to a rack. Do not taste the raw dough; it has raw egg and flour.

freezer.text: Freeze baked cookies up to 3 months, or freeze scoops of dough and bake from frozen, adding 1 to 2 minutes.

recipes.kids: Kids can scoop the dough. Whole nuts and seeds are a choking risk for children under 4; chop them fine or leave them out.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend and oats labeled gluten-free.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a batch; freeze dough balls.

recipes.name: Moroccan-Style Chicken with Apricots and Chickpeas
recipes.summary: Chicken thighs simmered with warm spices, dried apricots and chickpeas, served over couscous with toasted almonds.
equipment: large deep skillet or Dutch oven with lid
steps: Season the chicken with the salt. Heat the oil in the pan over medium-high heat and brown the chicken in two batches, about 5 minutes each. Move to a plate. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Lower the heat to medium. Cook the onion 5 minutes, then the garlic, ginger, cumin, cinnamon, paprika and turmeric for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, broth, chickpeas and apricots and scrape up the browned bits. Return the chicken with its juices.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes, until the chicken is tender and a thermometer reads 165°F. Stir in the lemon juice.
Meanwhile cook the couscous. Serve the chicken over couscous, topped with almonds and cilantro.
recipes.make_ahead: Make up to 3 days ahead; the flavor improves. Add the almonds when serving.

freezer.text: Freeze the chicken stew (without couscous) up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and pack with couscous for lunch.

recipes.kids: The spices are warm, not hot. Whole nuts and seeds are a choking risk for children under 4; chop them fine or leave them out.

swaps.gluten_free: Serve over rice or quinoa instead of couscous, and use gluten-free broth.

recipes.name: Date and Cashew Energy Bites
recipes.summary: No-bake bites of dates, cashews, oats, chia and flax rolled in coconut. Naturally sweet.
steps: Check the dates for pits. If they are dry, soak them in hot water 10 minutes, then drain.
Pulse the cashews and oats in the food processor until finely chopped.
Add the dates, chia, flax, cocoa, vanilla and salt. Process until the mixture holds together when pressed, adding a teaspoon of water if needed.
Roll into 1-inch balls and roll in coconut if you like. Chill 30 minutes to firm up.

freezer.text: Freeze up to 3 months; eat straight from the freezer or thaw 10 minutes.

recipes.kids: Kids can roll the balls. These are firm and sticky, so offer small pieces to young children.

swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of cashews.

recipes.name: Cashew Chicken
recipes.summary: Tender chicken, bell pepper and roasted cashews in a glossy garlic-ginger sauce, faster than takeout.
steps: Start the rice. Whisk the sauce ingredients in a small bowl.

Toss the chicken with 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Heat 1 tablespoon oil in the skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken, stirring, 5 to 6 minutes, until browned and a thermometer reads 165°F. Move to a plate. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Add the rest of the oil. Stir-fry the pepper and onion 3 minutes, then the garlic and ginger 30 seconds.
Stir the sauce, add it with the chicken and cook 1 to 2 minutes, until thick. Stir in the cashews and green onions. Serve over rice.
recipes.make_ahead: Cut the chicken and vegetables and mix the sauce up to 1 day ahead.

freezer.text: Freeze without the cashews up to 3 months; reheat to 165°F and add cashews.

leftovers.text: Pack with rice for lunch; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Whole nuts and seeds are a choking risk for children under 4; chop them fine or leave them out. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.gluten_free: Use tamari and a gluten-free hoisin.
swaps.nut_free: Use roasted sunflower seeds or leave the nuts out.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the chicken and vegetables; mix the sauce.

recipes.name: Curry Chicken Salad with Grapes and Cashews
recipes.summary: Shredded chicken in a light curry yogurt dressing with grapes, celery and cashews. Great in a wrap or on greens.
steps: Stir the yogurt, mayonnaise, curry powder, lemon juice, honey and salt in a large bowl.
Add the chicken, grapes, celery and green onions and stir to coat.
Fold in the cashews just before serving. Eat on greens, in wraps or on bread.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge; add the cashews the day you eat it. Use cooked chicken within 3 to 4 days of cooking.

leftovers.text: Pack in a lunchbox with an ice pack.

recipes.kids: Cut grapes into quarters for children under 4. Whole nuts and seeds are a choking risk for children under 4; chop them fine or leave them out.

swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of cashews.
swaps.gluten_free: Serve on greens or gluten-free bread.

prep_day.ahead: Shred the chicken; mix the dressing.

recipes.name: Asian Chicken Salad with Mandarins and Almonds
recipes.summary: Crunchy cabbage and romaine with chicken, mandarin oranges, toasted almonds and sesame seeds in a sesame-ginger dressing.
steps: Toast the almonds and sesame seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes, until golden. Cool.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Toss the cabbage, romaine, carrots, chicken and green onions with the dressing.
Top with the mandarin oranges, almonds and sesame seeds.
recipes.make_ahead: Keep the dressing, nuts and greens separate; they keep 3 days. The dressed salad holds 1 day.

leftovers.text: Pack dressing on the side for lunch.

recipes.kids: Whole nuts and seeds are a choking risk for children under 4; chop them fine or leave them out. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seeds instead of almonds.

prep_day.ahead: Slice the cabbage; toast nuts; mix dressing.

recipes.name: Homemade Hummus
recipes.summary: Smooth, lemony hummus from canned chickpeas and tahini in 10 minutes. Better than store-bought and cheaper.
steps: Process the tahini and lemon juice 1 minute, until thick and pale.
Add the garlic, cumin and salt and process 30 seconds.

Add the chickpeas and process 1 minute. With the machine running, add the cold water a tablespoon at a time until very smooth, about 2 minutes. Add a splash of the saved chickpea liquid if it is too thick.
Spread in a bowl, drizzle with olive oil and dust with paprika. Serve with vegetables or pita.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 5 days in the fridge, covered.

freezer.text: Freeze up to 3 months; stir well after thawing.

recipes.kids: Kids can push the button and pick dippers. Serve carrots as thin sticks for children under 4.

recipes.name: Cold Sesame Noodles
recipes.summary: Chilled noodles in a creamy tahini, soy and ginger sauce with crisp cucumber, carrots and sesame seeds.
steps: Cook the spaghetti in salted boiling water according to the package. Drain and rinse under cold water until cool.
Whisk the tahini, soy sauce, vinegar, honey, sesame oil, ginger, garlic and warm water until smooth.
Toss the noodles with the sauce, then add the cucumber, carrots and green onions.
Sprinkle with the sesame seeds. Serve cold or at room temperature.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge. Add a splash of water to loosen before serving.
recipes.kids: Kids can toss the noodles. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.meatless: It is already meatless; add cubed tofu or shredded chicken for more protein.

prep_day.ahead: Cook the noodles and mix the sauce.

recipes.name: Roasted Cauliflower with Lemon Tahini Sauce
recipes.summary: Deeply browned cauliflower drizzled with a creamy lemon-garlic tahini sauce and parsley.
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F.
Toss the cauliflower with the oil, cumin, salt and pepper and spread on the baking sheet with space between the pieces.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until deeply browned at the edges and tender.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt. Whisk in water until it pours like thick cream.
Drizzle the sauce over the warm cauliflower and sprinkle with parsley.
recipes.make_ahead: The sauce keeps 1 week in the fridge; thin with water.

leftovers.text: Toss leftovers into a grain bowl or wrap with the sauce.

recipes.kids: Kids can dip the florets in the sauce.

prep_day.ahead: Cut the florets; mix the sauce.

recipes.name: Pecan-Crusted Chicken Tenders
recipes.summary: Chicken tenders coated in ground pecans and panko and baked crisp. Serve with honey mustard.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Set the rack on the baking sheet and coat it with cooking spray.
Pulse the pecans in the food processor until they look like coarse crumbs. Mix with the panko, paprika and garlic powder in a shallow dish.
Put the flour in a second dish. Whisk the eggs and 1 tablespoon mustard in a third.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Dip each tender in flour, then egg, then press into the pecan mix. Set on the rack and spray the tops lightly. Wash your hands after handling raw chicken.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until golden and a thermometer in the thickest tender reads 165°F.
Stir the honey, mustard and mayonnaise (if using) together for dipping.
recipes.make_ahead: Coat the tenders up to 4 hours ahead and refrigerate on the rack.

freezer.text: Freeze baked tenders up to 3 months. Reheat at 400°F to 165°F, about 12 minutes.

leftovers.text: Slice over a salad or tuck into a wrap; reheat to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

swaps.gluten_free: Use gluten-free flour and gluten-free panko.
swaps.nut_free: Use all panko and add 2 tablespoons parmesan.

recipes.name: Sweet Potato Casserole with Pecan Topping
recipes.summary: Creamy mashed sweet potatoes under a crunchy brown sugar pecan streusel. A holiday side for any time.
steps: Cover the sweet potatoes with water in the pot and boil 15 to 18 minutes, until very tender. Drain well.
Heat the oven to 350°F and grease the baking dish.
Mash the sweet potatoes, then beat in the butter, brown sugar, eggs, milk, vanilla, cinnamon and salt until smooth. Spread in the dish.
Mix the pecans, brown sugar, flour and melted butter and sprinkle over the top.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the topping is golden and the center reaches 165°F.
recipes.make_ahead: Make the sweet potato base up to 2 days ahead and refrigerate. Add the topping and bake the day you serve it, adding about 10 minutes.

freezer.text: Freeze the unbaked base up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge, add topping and bake to 165°F.

recipes.kids: Kids can mash the potatoes and sprinkle the topping. Whole nuts and seeds are a choking risk for children under 4; chop them fine or leave them out.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend in the topping.
swaps.dairy_free: Use a plant milk and dairy-free butter.
swaps.nut_free: Use rolled oats instead of pecans.

prep_day.ahead: Boil and mash the sweet potatoes.

recipes.name: Pumpkin Oat Muffins with Pumpkin Seeds
recipes.summary: Spiced pumpkin muffins with oats and ground flax, topped with crunchy pumpkin seeds.
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F and line the muffin tin.
Whisk the pumpkin, eggs, oil, brown sugar and vanilla in a large bowl.
In another bowl mix the flour, oats, flax, baking soda, baking powder, spice and salt. Stir into the pumpkin mixture just until combined.
Fill the cups and sprinkle with the pumpkin seeds and sugar, pressing lightly.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out clean. Cool 5 minutes in the pan, then on a rack.
recipes.kids: Kids can sprinkle the seeds. Skip the seed topping on muffins for children under 4.

swaps.gluten_free: Use a gluten-free flour blend and oats labeled gluten-free.

recipes.name: Sunflower Crunch Chopped Salad
recipes.summary: Romaine, red cabbage, carrots and cucumber chopped small with sunflower and pumpkin seeds in a lemon-parmesan dressing.
steps: Rinse and dry the romaine, cabbage and cucumber.
Shake the dressing ingredients in a jar.
Chop the vegetables into small, even pieces and put them in a large bowl.
Toss with the dressing and top with the seeds just before serving.
recipes.make_ahead: Chopped vegetables keep 3 days in the fridge; dress and add the seeds when serving.
recipes.kids: Kids can shake the dressing jar. Leave the seeds off for children under 4. Honey is not safe for babies under 1 year old.

prep_day.ahead: Chop the vegetables; mix the dressing; keep the seeds separate.

recipes.name: Peanut Sweet Potato Stew
recipes.summary: A West African-style stew of sweet potatoes, chickpeas and greens in a creamy tomato and peanut butter broth.
steps: Heat the oil in the pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander and cayenne and cook 1 minute.
Add the sweet potatoes, tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of the hot broth until smooth, then stir it into the pot with the chickpeas.
Add the kale and simmer 5 minutes, until wilted. Stir in the salt and lime juice.
Serve over rice if you like, topped with chopped peanuts.
recipes.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; it thickens, so add a little broth when reheating to 165°F.

freezer.text: Freeze up to 3 months. Thaw in the fridge and reheat to 165°F.

leftovers.text: Reheat to 165°F and pack in a thermos.

recipes.kids: Leave out the cayenne for a mild stew. Whole nuts and seeds are a choking risk for children under 4; chop them fine or leave them out.

recipes.name: Classic Peanut Butter Cookies
recipes.summary: Soft, chewy peanut butter cookies with the classic fork crisscross on top.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F and line the baking sheets with parchment.
Beat the peanut butter, butter and both sugars until creamy. Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, baking soda and salt until a soft dough forms.
Roll into 1-inch balls and set 2 inches apart. Press each with a fork twice to make a crisscross.
Bake one sheet at a time, 9 to 11 minutes, until just set at the edges. Cool 5 minutes on the sheet, then on a rack. Do not taste the raw dough; it has raw egg and flour.

freezer.text: Freeze baked cookies or dough balls up to 3 months.

recipes.kids: Kids can roll the balls and press the fork marks.

swaps.nut_free: Use sunflower seed butter; the cookies may turn a little green inside, which is harmless.

prep_day.ahead: Bake a batch; freeze dough balls.
